hook: Born in a log cabin, he led the United States through its Civil War and ended slavery.

pages.x: Abraham Lincoln was born in 1809 in a one-room log cabin in Kentucky, and grew up on frontier farms in Indiana and Illinois. In all he had about one year of school, but he read every book he could borrow.
pages.img: Abraham Lincoln Birthplace National Historical Park

pages.x: He grew to 1.93 m, tall and strong from splitting logs for fences. In New Salem he was the local wrestling champion; the story goes that he lost only one of about 300 matches.

He worked as a shopkeeper, postmaster and surveyor, and taught himself law. People called him "Honest Abe": it was said he once walked miles to return a few cents of change. In 1837 he became a lawyer in Springfield.

In 1858 he said: "A house divided against itself cannot stand. I believe this government cannot endure, permanently half slave and half free." His debates on slavery with Stephen Douglas made him famous.

In 1860 an 11-year-old girl, Grace Bedell, wrote to him that he would look better with whiskers, as his face was so thin. He grew a beard, and when his train passed through her town, he asked to meet her.
He was elected president in 1860. Before he took office, seven Southern states left the Union to protect slavery. In April 1861 the Civil War began, the deadliest war in American history.
On 1 January 1863 he declared that the enslaved people in the rebel states were "forever free". Black men could now join the Union army, and nearly 200,000 did.
In November 1863, at the battlefield of Gettysburg, he gave a speech of just 272 words, promising that "government of the people, by the people, for the people, shall not perish from the earth."
In January 1865 he pushed the 13th Amendment to the Constitution through Congress, abolishing slavery in the whole country. On 9 April the main Southern army surrendered.
pages.img: Thirteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution

pages.x: Five days later, on 14 April 1865, he was shot at Ford's Theatre in Washington by the actor John Wilkes Booth. He died the next morning.
Lincoln held the United States together through its Civil War and ended slavery. Many historians rank him the greatest American president.
